findings.statement: CXCR2 is the top-ranked candidate but it is a neutrophil receptor: neutrophils make most of its inflamed-mucosa transcripts [gene=CXCR2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.965]. Smillie (no neutrophils) points to T/NK cells and the second dataset to myeloid cells, so the attribution is not replicated there. After composition adjustment only a small change remains, verdict partly_composition [gene=CXCR2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.4409]. It is best read as a marker of neutrophil influx; targeting it means targeting neutrophil recruitment.

CXCR1 behaves like CXCR2: neutrophils make nearly all of its transcripts in the Gubatan data, and the bulk increase largely disappears after adjustment, verdict partly_composition [gene=CXCR1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.5702]. The genetics and tractability support of the CXCR1-CXCR2 axis is real, but the bulk signal mostly tracks neutrophil arrival.

CXCL8 is made by macrophages and monocytes in Smillie and the second dataset agrees (myeloid), but with neutrophils included they make most of the transcripts [gene=CXCL8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.873]. The adjusted change is no longer significant, verdict composition [gene=CXCL8; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=0.0523]. It is a marker of myeloid/neutrophil influx rather than an intrinsic tissue change (adjustment may over-correct activation).

S100A8 is made almost entirely by myeloid cells and neutrophils contribute most of its transcripts [gene=S100A8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.909]. Part of the change survives adjustment, verdict partly_composition [gene=S100A8; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.9231]. A neutrophil-influx marker with some activation component.

CD274 (PD-L1) is attributed to myeloid cells (replicated), but neutrophil states carry much of it [gene=CD274; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.687]. A significant change remains after adjustment, partly_composition [gene=CD274; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.4978]. Its high rank rests on genetics and drug availability; the direction for therapy (checkpoint agonism vs blockade) is not resolved by expression data.

IDO1 comes from myeloid cells (macrophages, DC1; replicated in the second dataset), with a small neutrophil contribution [gene=IDO1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.072]. The change stays clearly significant after adjustment, partly_composition [gene=IDO1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.8505]. This supports a genuine activation change in resident myeloid cells and enterocytes, not neutrophil influx.

MMP1 is a stromal product, mainly inflammatory fibroblasts, replicated in the second dataset; the retained change after adjustment is large [gene=MMP1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.2636]. In Visium deconvolution inflammatory fibroblasts explain most of the in-situ signal [gene=MMP1; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.579]. CosMx detects it only at background, so single-cell spatial confirmation is lacking.

DUOX2 is epithelial (enterocytes), replicated in the second dataset, with almost no neutrophil contribution [gene=DUOX2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.947]. Its rise is intrinsic to the tissue after adjustment, though flagged partly_composition [gene=DUOX2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3161]. A tissue-intrinsic epithelial response, not influx.

CHI3L1 is stromal, from inflammatory fibroblasts, in both datasets [gene=CHI3L1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.941]. A large change survives adjustment [gene=CHI3L1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3967]. Neutrophils also contribute a sizeable share in the Gubatan data, so some signal is mixed.

AQP9 is overwhelmingly a neutrophil gene in the Gubatan data, and the adjusted change is much smaller than the unadjusted one [gene=AQP9; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.8551]. A neutrophil-influx marker.

caveats: Composition adjustment can over-correct because lineage scores also rise when resident cells activate; a lost signal (CXCL8) is not proof of pure influx, and a retained one is strong evidence of a tissue change.
Smillie 2019 did not capture neutrophils, so neutrophil genes (CXCR2) are misattributed to T/NK or macrophages there; the neutrophil view comes from Gubatan 2026 only.

Shares compare cell types, not tissue abundance. Spatial evidence was run only for MMP1 (Visium, CosMx at background, not on Xenium); other candidates (e.g. MMP3, IL1B, TREM1, LCN2) were screened only via neutrophil share, not composition.
Many other highly ranked genes are not covered individually here; no composition result was obtained for CXCL1, MMP3, IL1B or TREM1.
